summary: Meta's Alexandr Wang describes Muse Spark 1.3 as a step up over Muse Spark 1.2 on reasoning and coding, using fewer tool calls and tokens while better retaining requirements on long-horizon tasks.

mechanisms.reason: The post states a specific reduction in tool calls and tokens needed per task compared to the prior version.
mechanisms.quote: wastes fewer turns, uses ~20% fewer tool calls, ~25% fewer tokens, and holds onto requirements well during long-horizon tasks

practices.reason: A quantified version-over-version improvement in reasoning, coding, and task-completion efficiency would change which model an engineering team routes agentic workloads to.
practices.quote: It's a step up on reasoning and coding. compared to Muse Spark 1.2, Muse Spark 1.3 wastes fewer turns, uses ~20% fewer tool calls, ~25% fewer tokens, and holds onto requirements well during long-horizon tasks.
